title: card
description: One memory fact a learner is scheduled on: one row per (user, unlocked item, card kind). Minted when the lesson that unlocks the item is completed, from that lesson's srs.introduces_cards[] entry fanned out one row per card_type — 4,133 cards over 322 lessons, 9,453 card instances, no item enrolled twice anywhere. RUNTIME class: minted per learner, never committed to this repo. This record is a version-tagged DERIVED CACHE: every scheduling field on it can be recomputed by replaying the card's review_log rows, which is what makes an FSRS version bump or a re-optimized weight vector a replay rather than a migration. See design/user_state.md §5.

x-yomineko.note: card_id is COMPOSED from ids that already exist — f"{user_id}:{deck}:{item}:{kind}" — so no counter and no server round-trip is needed to name a card. It parses back by splitting on ':' into exactly seven segments, because user_id, deck and item are two segments each and kind is one; no corpus stable id carries a second colon (verified across corpus/**). Putting `deck` in the key means a refile is a migration, not an edit: see design/user_state.md §2.

card_id.description: f"{user_id}:{deck}:{item}:{kind}" — e.g. `usr:7f3a91:deck:vocab-n5:vocab:1580640:recognition`. The pattern is the composition rule made enforceable; the four components are also stored as their own fields below, because an index on a substring is not an index.

deck.description: The SRS deck this card lands in, copied from the minting lesson. A deck's `level` is a CURRICULUM POSITION, not a JLPT claim about its contents: filing follows the lesson's level, not the item's, and 23 cards already sit in a deck whose level differs from the item's own corpus level. Vocabulary owner: design — design/unlock_enums.json#deck. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

item.description: The corpus record this card tests, by published stable id. `vocab:` ids are SLUGS (`vocab:1580640`), never headwords — a headword is not an address, 93 of them are shared by 193 records. `kana:` is accepted at BOTH granularities: the family form `kana:hiragana-a` (57 cards today) and the glyph form `kana:hiragana-あ` (211 glyph records already exist and validate_srs_decks already accepts them). W29 migrates 57 -> 211 under decision D6; the contract has to hold across that migration, so it validates both. `sent:` becomes reachable when deck:phrases is populated (W30).

kind.description: What is being retrieved. All five kinds are contracted and nothing here marks production as phase 2: the export declares `production` on all 4,133 cards, so design/srs_design.md §6's "recognition-only at launch" is stale (design/user_state.md §10.1). `listening` is legal and has zero cards until audio lands (W35). Vocabulary owner: design — design/unlock_enums.json#card_type. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

cloze_target.description: `<sentence stable id>#<token index>` — which token of which sentence is blanked. REQUIRED when kind is `cloze` and null otherwise (enforced by the branch below). Required rather than optional because re-picking the sentence at review time silently changes the fact being tested, and a card whose content moves is not one memory fact: its difficulty and stability estimates become noise.

introduced_by.description: The lesson whose srs.introduces_cards[] minted this card. It is also the route a leech takes back to remediation, which is the only reason the app can answer "where did I learn this".

state.description: FSRS-6 card state. Neutral English per design/i18n.md — the learner-facing labels are pt-BR content, not enum values. Vocabulary owner: design — design/user_state.md#5-card. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

step.description: Position in the learning or relearning steps. Null outside those two states.

stability.description: FSRS S, in days: the interval at which recall probability falls to the desired retention. Derived from the review history, never authored. Null while state is `new`.

difficulty.description: FSRS D. Derived from the review history, never authored. Null while state is `new`.

reps.description: Total reviews. UX only — not an FSRS input.

lapses.description: Times this card was rated Again from `review`. UX only as far as the scheduler is concerned, but it drives the R33 furigana fade and the leech rule.

suspended_at.description: Out of the queue indefinitely — learner action, or the leech rule.

buried_until.description: Out of the queue until this instant. Sibling burying: seeing the recognition card should not hand you the answer to the production card an hour later.

leech_state.description: The remediation hook. design/srs_design.md §6 leaves leeches as an open owner question and no design doc carries a field for them; this is it. Vocabulary owner: design — design/user_state.md#5-card. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

tags.description: Corpus-derived card tags (homophone, homograph, confusable, irregular-reading — W28) plus learner-added ones. This is what an Anki-grade user filters, suspends and buries by, and no field for it exists anywhere in the corpus today. Deliberately NOT an enum: the learner-added half is open by construction.

fsrs_version.description: Which algorithm produced the cached state/stability/difficulty/due. Vocabulary owner: design — design/user_state.md#3-what-fsrs-6-actually-needs-and-why-card-is-a-cache. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

params_version.description: Which weight vector produced them. A card whose params_version is behind the user's is STALE, not wrong — recompute it lazily on the next review rather than rewriting every row on an optimizer run.
